stories.title: NEXTDC upgrades FY27 guidance as Scroggie takes responsibility for M3 delay
stories.summary: Australian data center operator NEXTDC has raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to AU$485-500 million following stronger-than-expected sales performance outside its troubled M3 Melbourne project. CEO Craig Scroggie has taken personal accountability for power supply delays and community engagement failures that have stalled the M3 development.
stories.why_it_matters: Scroggie's public accountability and the upgraded guidance signal operational resilience that may restore investor confidence after a governance setback, while the M3 power constraints highlight broader infrastructure bottlenecks facing Australian operators as they compete for energy-intensive AI workloads against a constrained grid.
stories.title_zh: NEXTDC上调FY27指引，Scroggie就M3项目延期承担责任
stories.summary_zh: 澳大利亚数据中心运营商NEXTDC在M3 Melbourne项目以外的销售业绩超预期后，将2027财年营收指引上调至4.85-5亿澳元。CEO Craig Scroggie对导致M3开发停滞的电力供应延迟和社区参与不足问题承担了个人责任。
stories.why_zh: Scroggie的公开问责和指引上调显示了运营韧性，可能在治理受挫后恢复投资者信心，而M3的电力限制凸显了澳大利亚运营商在能源密集型AI工作负载竞争中面临的更广泛基础设施瓶颈，背景是电网容量受限。
stories.content:
NEXTDC has raised its FY27 revenue and earnings guidance after reporting stronger sales growth outside its delayed M3 Melbourne development, while CEO Craig Scroggie has acknowledged the company’s responsibility for the project’s power and community engagement problems.

The data centre operator on 20 November upgraded its FY27 net revenue guidance to AU$485 million-AU$500m, from AU$475m-AU$500m, and underlying EBITDA guidance to AU$260m-AU$275m, from AU$245m-AU$265m.

The revised forecasts remain below the original guidance issued in August, which included revenue and earnings from customer contracts at M3. Those contracts, representing approximately AU$140m each in net revenue and underlying EBITDA in the original forecast, remain excluded while NEXTDC assesses when the affected capacity can be delivered and its financial contribution reliably estimated.

The exclusion also covers M3 capacity that is already billing. NEXTDC said any service level credits payable on those contracts could reduce underlying EBITDA below the new range.

The company said the revenue upgrade reflected stronger sales and growth outside the affected M3 contracts, together with greater confidence in the timing of customer delivery. The higher EBITDA forecast mainly reflects savings from focusing operating expenditure on delivering capacity to customers, together with higher expected net revenue.

NEXTDC reaffirmed its FY27 capital expenditure guidance of AU$4.5bn-AU$5bn, unchanged from 21 October, following a review of its investment programme. The range is AU$750m, or 13-14 percent, below the original August guidance of AU$5.25bn-AU$5.75bn. Excluding about AU$230m of capitalised interest, which the August figure did not include, the reduction is around AU$980m, or 17-19 percent, on a like-for-like basis.

### Hard year

Addressing shareholders at the company’s annual general meeting, Scroggie described it as the hardest of his 15 AGMs as CEO and accepted responsibility for the delays at M3.

“As CEO, I am accountable for delivery. Power, planning approvals, construction and community support are all part of delivery. We rely on partners for each of them, and they have their own responsibilities. That does not change mine,” he said.

“At M3 we needed to work more closely with our power and construction partners, and with the community. We are now doing that.”

The M3 expansion in West Footscray has been delayed by problems securing additional grid supply. The additional power requires electricity distributor Jemena to install new power lines, but residents raised concerns about the size of proposed power poles. Jemena subsequently suspended the works, citing safety concerns and a lack of access to work sites resulting from community opposition.

Scroggie said Jemena had recognised that its community engagement and consultation around the network upgrades had been insufficient and was strengthening its approach.

“Those concerns deserved to be heard earlier,” he said. “None of that changes where accountability sits. The upgrade serves our project and our customer. Delivering that project is our job, and I am accountable for it.”

### New options

NEXTDC and Jemena are now pursuing several options in parallel to bring power to M3, including alternative routes through industrial streets or underground, alternative substations, upgrades to existing feeders and broader grid options.

Jemena will lead any community consultation and approvals process once its technical solution has been finalised, with NEXTDC saying it will support the process. Scroggie said the company would provide a further update at its half-year results in February, or earlier if there was material progress.

Construction is continuing on the approved development of contracted capacity at M3, and the affected customer contracts remain in place, subject to the customer’s rights. However, the previously announced delay relates to the timing of the next increase in power supply to M3.

### Community committee

The company is also changing its approach to community engagement. It is establishing a Community Consultative Committee at M3 and developing a formal engagement plan for the site, and has launched dedicated contact channels and introduced defined response times for complaints and enquiries. NEXTDC plans to develop community engagement plans for all its sites in Australia and Asia.

“We build on industrial land, close to power, network connectivity and our customers,” Scroggie said. “In the past we relied on formal council and state planning processes to set the standard and own the conversation with the community. That is no longer enough.”

“We will now engage earlier and directly, alongside our power and construction partners,” he said.

The capital expenditure review has reinforced a shift away from discretionary development towards completing contracted projects. NEXTDC said most of its FY27 capital spending will be directed towards existing customer commitments at S4 Sydney, M2 and M3 Melbourne, and KL1 Kuala Lumpur.

Uncontracted developments, including M4, M5, S5, S7, GC1 and AK1, as well as new land acquisitions, remain on hold. Future investment will be considered on a project-by-project basis, with NEXTDC requiring customer contracts, returns above its cost of capital, sufficiently advanced power and planning arrangements, and funding in place.

### S4 update

The company’s largest contracted development is S4 in western Sydney, which has 250MW of its planned 365MW IT load contracted. Construction is under way on the first 115MW phase, which is expected to begin billing in FY28. Phase 2 remains in the NSW planning process.

NEXTDC said it had a forward order book of 565MW on a pro forma basis at 30 June 2026, including the affected M3 contracts. Scroggie said demand for high-quality, secure and reliable data centre capacity was the strongest he had seen during his time as CEO, with cloud computing and AI continuing to drive demand.

“Demand is not our constraint. Delivery is,” he told shareholders.

The company also said it had sufficient funding to deliver its existing contracted customer capacity and did not expect to raise capital from shareholders for that work at this time. It is continuing to explore capital recycling options, including a potential joint venture structure for S4.

The company said it would prioritise converting contracted capacity into revenue and operating cash flow, rather than committing capital to uncontracted projects. “The rest of the business is performing. FY26 was a record year,” Scroggie said.

NEXTDC operates 18 data centres across Australia and Malaysia and has five sites in development. Its development pipeline exceeds 5GW across Australia and international markets, although uncontracted development projects are currently on hold while the company focuses on delivering its forward order book.

“Outside M3, the business is performing, and demand is the strongest I have seen. Our job is to deliver the value in this business for our shareholders,” he concluded.

stories.title: Most firms favour on-premises AI, Schneider survey finds
stories.summary: With deployment hurdles still biting, 55% of enterprises now plan to own at least part of their AI infrastructure, a Schneider survey found.
stories.title_zh: Schneider调查发现多数企业倾向本地部署AI
stories.content:
Fri, 20th Nov 2026 (Today)
Schneider Electric has published global research showing that most enterprises prefer on-premises infrastructure for artificial intelligence deployments. The survey found that 55% plan to own at least part of their AI infrastructure.

The study, conducted by Omdia on behalf of Schneider Electric, gathered responses from enterprise leaders across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific on AI strategy, adoption, spending, infrastructure and returns. It suggests AI use is moving beyond experimentation, while companies weigh compliance, privacy and operational demands when deciding where to run workloads.

Across the sample, 35% of respondents said increased productivity was the main reason for adopting more AI. A further 25% cited cost reduction, while 22% pointed to time savings.

The findings suggest pilot activity is already widespread. Nearly three-quarters of respondents said they are running five or more proofs of concept, 63% said they plan to deploy generative AI applications, and 23% said AI models are already adding value within their organisations.

Returns are also beginning to emerge. Among companies with implemented AI projects, 60% said return on investment was meeting or exceeding expectations. That included 29% reporting returns of two to five times and 17% reporting returns of five to 10 times.

Budgets are rising as that pattern takes hold. More than half of respondents said their AI budgets for 2026 were above USD $500,000, while 31% put spending above USD $1 million. Some 78% expect AI budgets to rise in the following year, with nearly 30% forecasting year-on-year growth of 11% to 25%.

### Infrastructure choices

The research indicates that enterprises are not relying solely on public cloud or outsourced environments as budgets grow. It found that 55% preferred company-owned, on-premises infrastructure for AI, citing data privacy and security, reliability requirements, and regulatory compliance as the main reasons.

That preference reflects wider concerns about data handling and control in regulated sectors such as healthcare, financial services, life sciences, government, education and manufacturing, all of which were represented in the survey. Respondents also included executives from IT, product engineering, research and development, and general management.

At the same time, companies are encountering practical limits as they try to move projects into production. More than half of respondents said no more than one in five proofs of concept reach production because of human and infrastructure barriers.

A lack of in-house expertise was cited by 33% of respondents as an obstacle to full-scale deployment. Another 32% pointed to integration problems with existing systems and architectural complexity.

New infrastructure brings another layer of difficulty. When deploying new systems for AI, respondents most often named scaling AI IT clusters, costs, and sourcing power and cooling infrastructure as their top challenges.

Those issues appear to be pushing organisations towards outside help. The survey found that 59% rely on external partners to help shape AI strategy, while 67% depend on outside support for implementation.

### Skills gap

The partner mix spans cloud providers, infrastructure vendors, software platforms, systems integrators and specialist AI firms. This suggests companies are assembling broad supplier networks to bridge skills shortages and reduce deployment complexity.

Paul Tyrer, Global Vice President, AI Ecosystem, at Schneider Electric, said the results show a shift in enterprise priorities as AI projects mature.

"As AI moves from experimentation to real-world application, enterprises are focused on making these technologies deliver measurable business value at the right speed, accuracy and cost," Tyrer said.

"This research from Schneider Electric and Omdia highlights both the opportunities and the challenges organisations face as they formulate and implement AI strategies and supportive technologies. Understanding where organisations are making progress and where they need support is critical to helping them move forward with confidence."

Omdia said the survey also points to a recurring delivery problem, with many organisations unable to convert early testing into wider deployment. That gap is feeding demand for reference designs, validated architectures and implementation support.

"As enterprises work to develop and manage their own AI environments, the lack of internal expertise remains a significant barrier and a leading reason proofs of concept fail," said Maxine Holt, Vice President, Enterprise & Channel Research, at Omdia.

"By leveraging existing partners and resources such as reference designs and validated architectures, organisations can navigate the complexity of AI infrastructure while aligning investment with deployment needs and accelerating time to adoption and business value."

stories.title: NVIDIA's Deb Shoquist details AI supply chain challenge
stories.summary: Nvidia operations executive Deb Shoquist has outlined the severe supply chain scaling challenges confronting AI infrastructure deployment, emphasizing dependencies on suppliers capable of rapid capacity expansion and technological adaptation. The constraints affect everything from advanced packaging to power delivery systems required for next-generation GPU clusters.
stories.why_it_matters: Shoquist's candid assessment validates industry concerns that physical infrastructure bottlenecks—not just chip fabrication—will throttle AI capacity growth, giving vertically integrated operators with direct supplier relationships and capital depth a structural advantage over smaller colocation providers competing for scarce components and skilled integration labor.
stories.title_zh: NVIDIA的Deb Shoquist详述AI供应链挑战
stories.summary_zh: Nvidia运营高管Deb Shoquist概述了AI基础设施部署面临的严峻供应链扩展挑战，强调了对能够快速扩大产能和技术适应的供应商的依赖。这些制约影响着从先进封装到下一代GPU集群所需电力输送系统的各个环节。
stories.why_zh: Shoquist的坦率评估证实了行业担忧：物理基础设施瓶颈——不仅仅是芯片制造——将制约AI产能增长，这使拥有直接供应商关系和资本深度的垂直整合运营商在争夺稀缺组件和熟练集成劳动力方面，比小型colocation提供商具有结构性优势。
stories.content:
Fri, 20th Nov 2026 (Today)
NVIDIA has highlighted the role of Deb Shoquist in managing the manufacturing and supply chain behind its artificial intelligence products. She recently received the 2026 Dr. Lisa Su Woman of Innovation Award.

Shoquist oversees operations at the US chip designer, working with a network of manufacturers and suppliers that includes TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, SPIL, King Yuan Electronics, Unimicron, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor.

Her remarks offer a view into how NVIDIA manages production as it has expanded from selling chips to building broader data-centre systems and platforms. They also show how heavily the company relies on long-standing manufacturing relationships in Asia and the US as demand for its AI products remains high.

Shoquist described the job in simple terms, while stressing the challenge of matching designs with suppliers that can deliver at scale.

"At the most basic level, our job is to convert designs into the physical world. Our design team creates a blueprint, and our job is to transition it into a reliable, high-performance supply chain. A matchmaker is probably the best analogy. You have to find the partner that matches your ramp style and has the technology that can meet the needs of very precise designs. The supplier has to be financially strong enough to invest in our ramps. They have to be highly technical. And they have to be willing to do something that has never been done before. If you don't have all three, you can't create products at the volume and speed that we need. You need those three legs, and in some cases, if you only have two, you have to invest in the company to make them a partner," said Deb Shoquist, Operations Executive, NVIDIA.

### Growing network

NVIDIA's manufacturing base has developed over decades. TSMC has worked with NVIDIA since 1998, while SPIL and King Yuan Electronics were assembling and testing its chips more than 20 years ago.

That network has had to widen as NVIDIA moved beyond semiconductors into larger integrated systems. Shoquist said the shift has taken the company into newer technology segments where suppliers may have the technical expertise, but not yet the factory scale or financial resources needed for rapid growth.

"When we were primarily a chip manufacturer, we were small, and the semiconductor industry was at scale. In that environment, it was about picking the best technology match for the products we envisioned. As we became a data center systems company, we needed more partners. But we've also now entered into new technology areas where the scale of the supply base is still developing. For example, our optical component partners have the technology and the willingness, but they don't yet have the scale or capital to build fabs for the volume we need. To grow, we needed to support and invest, like we did with Coherent and Lumentum. Beyond that, with products like CPO (co-packaged optics), we're creating entirely new supply chains with scale partners that are new to the optics world. Leading the integration of talent across the supply chain is the key to driving this incredible technology to high volume quickly," said Shoquist.

She also pointed to the importance of relationships on factory floors, not just in executive offices. According to Shoquist, years of working directly with production staff have made it easier for suppliers to raise concerns about engineering support, quality staffing, automation and material buffers.

"Over 20 years, you meet many individuals key to the success of your supply. You meet not only the CEOs, but also the people that are running the production floor. These are the people that really know the problems of manufacturing. If you don't have a tight working relationship with the people deeper in the organization, then it's hard to have an open dialogue about any challenges. But when you have tight relationships, they want to help you, and they feel comfortable enough telling you, 'I need better technical support on the floor. I need more quality engineers. We need a better design. We need to automate this. We need more buffers of material.' That's what 20 years of working with our suppliers has taught us. It's year after year of learning from people, getting to know people deeper in the organization and creating the trust where they can tell us what we need to do to be successful with them," said Shoquist.

### Pressure points

One of the clearest signals in her account was the central role of chip supply from TSMC. Shoquist said NVIDIA tracks each chip from die identification number to customer invoice and allocates output based on weekly factory performance.

"You need to first understand what the most critical components are, and protect and prioritize production around them. We need wafers like we need air. And the critical component is the TSMC chip. As it comes out of assembly every week, we decide what factory gets what chip. Every week, we look at factory performance. If a particular factory yield is low, if their time of ownership is not at the level we want, they don't get more chips that week. We keep track of every chip, from the identification number on the die all the way to the customer invoice. If you want to be our supplier, you have to support that traceability process. With that process, we took the time it takes from chip out at TSMC to system out at Foxconn and Wistron from five to two weeks when supply and demand requires it. Think of the supply chain as a large circulatory system with pathways everywhere - and when you need to accelerate any branch of it, you have the power to do that. We have the capability to do that. It's empowering and exciting," said Shoquist.

She also described a production problem during the ramp-up of the compute board for NVIDIA GB200 systems. An automated test process fell well below expected throughput, prompting the operations team in Taiwan to switch back to manual loading and bring in hundreds of operators to maintain shipments.

This was followed by a broader effort involving design engineering, industrial operations, product engineering, test engineering and Foxconn's automation engineers to redesign the line before full-scale production.

"We were getting ready to go to volume production with Foxconn and Wistron for the compute board of NVIDIA GB200. The last step in the process was a test managed by an automated handler - a completely new approach for us, developed to meet the demands of high-volume throughput for these complicated products. During the initial ramp, the throughput was significantly below plan. The Operations Director of Taiwan Manufacturing made the call that to protect the product and shipments, he needed to disable the entire process and return to manual test loading. Our manufacturers backed him without question and brought in the necessary manpower to meet the immediate needs, literally hundreds of operators. That kept production moving, but would not solve the throughput requirement of full production. As with any operations problem, the root cause had many elements to it: test tray assembly, test tray design, automation hardware design, automation control software, product yield. From all viewpoints, it was a difficult problem to resolve quickly. That's when we executed the NVIDIA swarm. Teams from NVIDIA design engineering, operations industrial, and product and test engineering, as well as from Foxconn automation engineering, flooded the line with talent to redesign and reactivate the line before the scale ramp hit. This is not an unusual occurrence when there is a problem in operations. All teams at NVIDIA are street fighters - action-oriented, and know no organizational boundaries. We say that 'the mission is the boss,' but we also live 'the mission is the boss,'" said Shoquist.

stories.title: Ecolab launches cooling platform for AI data centres
stories.summary: The new system aims to improve reliability and cut water and energy use as data centres race to cool denser AI workloads.
stories.title_zh: Ecolab推出面向AI数据中心的冷却平台
stories.content:
Fri, 20th Nov 2026 (Today)
Ecolab has launched an integrated cooling platform for AI data centres, combining liquid cooling hardware, fluid management and digital monitoring in a single offering.

The platform links CoolIT's direct liquid cooling equipment with Ecolab's fluid management technology, software and service network. At the centre is Ecolab's 3D TRASAR technology, integrated into the CoolIT CHx 3000, a 3-megawatt coolant distribution unit.

The combined setup is designed to give operators real-time visibility into cooling system performance. It aims to help data centre operators improve reliability, manage water and energy use, and increase computing density as AI workloads grow.

The launch marks a further step in Ecolab's effort to build a larger business around AI infrastructure and the broader high-tech supply chain. Its activities in that market already include ultrapure water systems for semiconductor manufacturing through Ovivo Electronics, as well as water and process technologies used in power generation.

Cooling has become a bigger issue for data centre operators as AI systems require more densely packed computing equipment and higher power loads. Direct liquid cooling is attracting more attention across the sector because it can remove heat more efficiently than traditional air-based systems in high-density environments.

Christophe Beck, Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer of Ecolab, said the company sees an opportunity to bring together parts of the cooling process that have often been managed separately.

"AI is advancing at an extraordinary pace, and the infrastructure behind it needs to advance just as fast," Beck said. "That's exactly what we're enabling today. For too long, cooling hardware, fluid management and digital technology have operated separately. We're bringing them together to help our customers get more computing power, faster, while using less water and energy. And we're just getting started."

### Growth plans

The product launch comes as Ecolab outlines broader ambitions for its high-tech business. That unit is growing by more than 25% annually and is approaching USD $1.5 billion in 2026 annualised sales, including Ovivo and CoolIT.

Ecolab is targeting USD $4 billion in annual high-tech sales by 2030, with operating income margins of 25%. The figures point to a push beyond its more established markets in water, hygiene and infection prevention into areas more directly tied to AI infrastructure demand.

Ecolab generates USD $16 billion in annual sales, employs 48,000 people and serves customers in more than 170 countries and 40 industries. Its work spans food, hospitality, healthcare, data centres, microelectronics and life sciences.

### Water focus

Ecolab has also sought to position itself around the water demands linked to AI. That includes supplying ultrapure water for chip manufacturing, providing water-related systems that support electricity generation, and offering direct liquid cooling technologies for high-density computing.

That pitch reflects a wider industry debate about the environmental footprint of AI infrastructure, particularly electricity consumption and water use. Data centre operators and suppliers are under pressure to show that rising computing demand can be matched with more efficient use of resources.

The new platform is intended to address both pressures through tighter management of coolant systems and more direct insight into performance at the equipment level. Integrating monitoring into the coolant distribution unit is meant to give operators a clearer real-time view of how cooling systems are running.

The move also underlines the role of acquisitions in Ecolab's strategy. CoolIT has given the company a route into direct liquid cooling hardware, while Ovivo Electronics has extended its reach in semiconductor water treatment, bringing Ecolab into another critical part of the AI infrastructure chain.

stories.title: PDG and Stockland file to develop Sydney data centers
stories.summary: Princeton Digital Group and Australian property developer Stockland have jointly submitted development applications for new data center projects in Sydney. The partnership combines PDG's specialized data center expertise with Stockland's extensive land holdings and development capabilities in the Australian market.
stories.why_it_matters: The PDG-Stockland alliance exemplifies how international operators are penetrating supply-constrained Australian markets through local property partnerships, accelerating project timelines while potentially intensifying competition for power allocations and skilled construction labor in a market already struggling with M3-style delays.
stories.title_zh: PDG和Stockland申请开发Sydney数据中心
stories.summary_zh: Princeton Digital Group与澳大利亚房地产开发商Stockland已联合提交在悉尼开发新数据中心项目的申请。该合作将PDG的专业数据中心经验与Stockland在澳大利亚市场的大量土地储备和开发能力相结合。
stories.why_zh: PDG与Stockland的合作 exemplifies 国际运营商如何通过本地房地产合作伙伴关系进入供应受限的澳大利亚市场，在加速项目时间线的同时，可能加剧本已面临M3式延迟困境的市场中对电力配额和熟练建筑劳动力的竞争。
stories.content:
Applications have been filed to develop more data centers around Sydney, Australia.

APAC data center firm Princeton Digital Group (PDG) has filed to develop its first Australian campus in Campbelltown.

Aussie real estate firm Stockland, meanwhile, has filed to develop a data center in Wetherill Park and expanded the scope of a planned project in Kemps Creek.

## PDG files for 100MW data center in Campbelltown

PDG has filed a SEARS application with the New South Wales government for the 192 Narellan Road Data Center outside Sydney, in Campbelltown.

The campus is located on 12.7 hectares of undeveloped land within the Maryfields Estate, approximately 44 kilometres southwest of the Sydney Central Business District.

This would be PDG’s first project in Australia.

Codenamed Project Genesis, the project would total two buildings – a two-story facility and a three-story building – and an on-site substation. On-site rooftop solar panels and a battery energy storage system (BESS) are also planned.

Documents suggest PDG is working with Sydney-based real estate firm Morehuman Property Group, a company traditionally focused on residential and hotel developments.

The Franciscan Order of Friars Minor sold the site in 2020 to Uniting Care for around AU$18.5m. The land was previously earmarked for a senior living development comprising 500 dwellings and 200 aged care beds, and part of a larger development known as Maryfields Estate, which would have included a business park.

PDG was founded in 2017 and has data centers in operation or development across China, Singapore, India, Indonesia, South Korea, Malaysia, and Japan. The company says its portfolio totals 1.8GW.

## Stockland plans data center in Wetherill Park

Real estate firm Stockland is also set to develop another data center outside Sydney.

Stockland has filed a SEARS application to develop the Wetherill Park Data Center at 2 Davis Road in the Wetherill Park area of North Sydney, around 25 kilometres west of the Sydney CBD.

The project comprises a single four-story building totaling 38,090 sqm (409,997 sq ft) and an on-site substation. The 170MW building, set to feature 20 data halls, will use a closed-loop cooling system to reduce water use, along with air-cooled chillers.

Stockland is expecting the first 55MW to come online in Q1 2029, ramping up to 250MW of grid capacity by Q1 2031.

The site currently accommodates a warehouse and distribution facility built in the 1980s that is set to be demolished. The Holroyd Terminal Station is located approximately 700m northeast of the site.

Some AU$2.25 billion is set to be invested in the project.

Another data center is planned next door at 3 Davis Road. Known as the Davis Road Data Center or “Project Blue Tongue,” that 88MW development will comprise two three-story data center buildings, a two-story tape storage building, and an on-site substation.

## Stockland expands Kemps Creek projects

Stockland has also filed to expand a planned data center development in the Kemps Creek area of Sydney.

The company originally filed alongside investment firm Fife Capital in April to develop a single 168MW building at 90 Aldington Road in Kemps Creek that would total 14 data halls. The application included plans for a 1GW substation.

In an updated SEARS application, Stockland is now hoping to develop two buildings on 20 hectares at 74 – 88 Aldington Road, along with the 1GW substation known as the Ropes Creek switching station. The two multi-story data centers would total 365MW of IT capacity across a combined 86,355 sqm (929,517 sq ft).

“Since the issue of the previous SEARs for 90 Aldington Road in April 2026, the proposal has evolved substantially through the consolidation of Lots 43 and 90, refinement of the infrastructure strategy, and continued engagement with key agencies and infrastructure providers,” Stockland said in its filing.

Some AU$4.99 billion (US$3.35bn) is set to be invested in the project.

Founded in 1952, Sydney-based Stockland is one of Australia’s largest property groups. The company has recently begun focusing more on data center developments and has partnered with EdgeConneX.

The company has an existing data center in the Macquarie Park area of Sydney and is planning to expand in the area. It also has several developments in the works around Melbourne.

Stockland recently backed off from a planned project in the Cooks River area of Sydney

stories.title: ANZ migrates 1.7 petabytes of data to AWS
stories.summary: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Limited (ANZ) has completed a cloud migration effort to Amazon Web Services (AWS).
stories.title_zh: ANZ将1.7 PB数据迁移至AWS
stories.content:
Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Limited (ANZ) has completed a cloud migration effort to Amazon Web Services (AWS).

The company revealed earlier this week that it has migrated one of its largest data platforms to AWS, in total moving some 1.7 petabytes of data.

The migration was completed in six months, despite estimates expecting it to take 18 months, with the use of AI-assisted engineering to help with analyzing, converting, testing, and optimizing workloads. The bank said that engineers used a troubleshooting AI assistant powered by Amazon Bedrock to identify and fix performance bottlenecks using the chatbot, without needing to manually comb through code and configurations.

The new platform is hope to provide greater scalability and resilience to ANZ and enable the bank to improve customer and employee experience.

ANZ chief data and AI officer, Kai Yang, said: "Data is the foundation of modern banking and increasingly the foundation of AI. As we explore new ways to use data and analytics to improve customer and employee experiences, having modern, scalable and secure infrastructure is critical. This transformation modernizes one of ANZ's most important data platforms and provides a stronger foundation for future innovation. It gives us greater flexibility to scale and simplify our technology environment and accelerate the development of new data and capabilities over time."

AWS managing director for Australia and New Zealand, Chris Casey added: "Migrating a major banking data platform while it continues to serve customers in real time is one of the most complex undertakings in financial services. Completing a migration of this scale in six months reflects the trust and world-class delivery capability of AWS Professional Services, AWS Partners, and the team at ANZ."

ANZ is a known customer of IBM's mainframes, and according to an A.G.Coombs case study, has two data center facilities in Melbourne, Australia. In 2009, a 4,000 sqm (43,055 sq ft) data center was also listed in Highbrook, Auckland.

In its 2026 Annual Report, the bank noted that its technology expenses had decreased by $186 million (eight percent), which was "driven by ongoing technology simplification and lower amortization from change in useful lives of select strategic software assets, partially offset by inflationary impacts on vendor costs."

In 2025, AWS said it would invest $13bn in expanding its data center infrastructure in Australia.

Australia's CommBank and Westpac have both migrated significant workloads and data to the cloud provider.

stories.title: Data center powered by Huawei Ascend chips launches in China
stories.summary: A new data center has commenced operations in China utilizing Huawei's Ascend AI processors, marking a significant deployment of domestically developed chips amid ongoing US technology restrictions. The facility represents China's continued push to build AI infrastructure independent of American semiconductor supply chains.
stories.why_it_matters: Domestic Ascend-based deployments reduce China's vulnerability to US export controls but also signal to global operators that Chinese cloud providers may increasingly favor local silicon, reshaping procurement patterns and competitive dynamics for international chip vendors in the world's second-largest data center market.
stories.title_zh: 采用Huawei Ascend芯片的数据中心在China落地
stories.summary_zh: 一座采用Huawei Ascend AI处理器的新数据中心在中国投入运营，这标志着在美国技术限制背景下，国产芯片的一次重大部署。该设施代表了中国持续推动建设独立于美国半导体供应链的AI基础设施的努力。
stories.why_zh: 基于Ascend的国内部署降低了中国对美国出口管制的脆弱性，同时也向全球运营商发出信号：中国云服务商可能日益青睐本土芯片，这将重塑全球第二大数据中心市场中国际芯片供应商的采购模式和竞争格局。
stories.content:
As reported by the South China Morning Post, the data center is the country's first AI cluster of Huawei's Ascend 950DT chips and is located at China Telecom's submarine cable landing station in Shantou.

Huawei Ascend 950DT is a 2026 data center AI accelerator built on Huawei's Da Vinci v3 architecture for decode-stage inference and training, offering up to 2,007 TFLOPS (MXFP4) and 1,034 TFLOPS (FP8/MXFP8) with 144GB (or 96GB) of HiZQ 2.0 HBM (high-bandwidth memory) at 4Tbps.

The chips can scale to clusters of more than 128,000 cards.

The IT capacity and number of chips deployed at the site have not been disclosed.

The data center is designed for a "token export" business model, processes AI queries from foreign users, and began operating last week. IT services firm Guangdong Tianyima Information Industry operates the data center.

The project is the result of approximately $150 million in investment.

China Telecom's Shantou International Submarine Cable Landing Station was built between 1997 and 2001, and is one of China Telecom's three mainland landing stations.

According to TokenHeart, the computing infrastructure is described as 1+4, with the Shantou site aggregating compute power resources, and data centers in the Eastern Guangdong Information Building, Tuopu, Zhuchi, and Chaoshan providing capacity for elastic scheduling.

The publication reports that foreign demand at the site now exceeds three trillion tokens daily.

Another cluster of the Huawei chips - with 1,024 cards and liquid cooling technologies - went live in Shanghai in September, according to SCMP. In addition, DeepSeek is said to be planning to use the AI infrastructure at its data center planned in Inner Mongolia, China.

This month, a launch event was also held for a 10,000-chip AI cluster in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area powered by Alibaba's Zhenwu AI chips. The data center is owned and operated by China Telecom. It is ultimately planned to scale to 100,000 chips.

stories.title: OpenAI claims its models have delivered chip design improvements across both in-house and AMD-designed hardware
stories.summary: OpenAI has shared details about how chip engineers have used its large language models to improve chip design.
stories.title_zh: OpenAI称其模型在自研和AMD设计硬件上均实现芯片设计改进
stories.content:
OpenAI has shared details about how chip engineers have used its large language models to improve chip design.

In a blog post, the company said that in addition to using its models to boost development of its in-house custom inference chip, Jalapeño, OpenAI has also been working with AMD to deliver “significant gains on third-party hardware.”

OpenAI said it used GPT-o3 mini to help design Jalapeño in early 2025, with the model making “non-trivial PPA (power, performance, and area) improvements, including reducing standard-cell area in the vector unit by 13 percent and the matrix unit by ten percent.

While working with AMD, the generative AI giant said improvements of up to 14 percent had been realized, “relative to heavily optimized baselines on the flagship GPU IP.” The chip company also saw single-digit PPA percentage gains across key blocks of its upcoming CPU when using designs written by an OpenAI model.

An unspecified OpenAI model also identified further improvements by rewriting the code that describes the chip’s circuits (SystemVerilog RTL), the company claimed, noting that this is equivalent to a year's worth of progress being achieved in less than five months. AMD has reportedly included these changes in a recent chip design that is now in the manufacturing phase, and is planning to add further changes to production design files for future versions.

“Looking ahead, we expect further PPA improvements on top of GPU and CPU relative to the most optimized baseline,” OpenAI said.

Separately, the company said it tested five of its models – GPT-5.5, GPT-5.5 Sol, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and GPT-6.2 Astra – on two open-source 32-bit RISC-V cores in order to measure chip design capabilities across model generations.

Models were given an original hardware description for each core and asked to increase throughput, and then provided with written requirements and templates and asked to design a core based on those specifications. OpenAI said it found that all five models scored higher when they designed a core from written requirements than when they tried to improve the existing design.

Following these tests, OpenAI said it would be partnering with Synopsys to train GPT-Synopsys, a new model, to use Synopsys electronic design automation (EDA) tools in a way that mimics the process undertaken by chip engineers.

stories.title: Microsoft begins work on Westgate data center in New Zealand
stories.summary: Microsoft has commenced construction on its Westgate data center campus in Auckland, New Zealand, expanding its cloud infrastructure footprint in the region. The development represents a significant capital commitment by a major hyperscale provider to a relatively underserved Asia-Pacific market.
stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft's New Zealand investment validates the market's emergence from pandemic-delayed cloud adoption and will pressure local enterprises and government agencies to accelerate digital transformation, while potentially drawing competing hyperscalers to evaluate Auckland as a disaster recovery alternative to Australian facilities constrained by power and land availability.
stories.title_zh: Microsoft开始在新西兰Westgate建设data center
stories.summary_zh: Microsoft已开始在奥克兰建设其Westgate数据中心园区，扩大其在该地区的云基础设施布局。这一开发代表了主要hyperscale提供商对相对服务不足的亚太市场的重要资本承诺。
stories.why_zh: Microsoft在新西兰的投资验证了该国从疫情延迟的云采用中复苏，并将推动本地企业和政府机构加速数字化转型，同时可能吸引竞争hyperscale评估奥克兰作为受电力和土地可用性限制的澳大利亚设施的灾难恢复替代方案。
stories.content:
Works on Microsoft's Westgate data center in New Zealand have begun.

According to the company's project overview page, construction works started in September of this year.

The company said that "current and upcoming works include site establishment, piling, earthworks, excavation, concrete works, crane activity, and deliveries."

According to the project page, the data center site is being accessed from Kakano Road.

According to Facebook posts from Stop Data Centres Auckland, the project is located at 7 Kakano Road with an entrance at 85 Rotu Drive.

Details about the data center have not been provided, but it seems to be an expansion of the company's existing cloud region in the country.

First announced in May 2020 and receiving approval in September of that year, Microsoft's New Zealand cloud region launched in December 2024.

In 2022, the company revealed that the cloud region would be powered by 100 percent renewable energy, later signing a 51.4MW ten-year geothermal PPA with Contact Energy for the Te Huka 3 power station.

*DCD* has contacted Microsoft for further information.

stories.title: Tesla unveils Powercore solid-state transformer platform aimed at data centers
stories.summary: Electric vehicle and energy storage manufacturer Tesla has unveiled a new medium-voltage platform, with data centers among its target markets.
stories.title_zh: Tesla发布面向data center的Powercore solid-state transformer平台
stories.content:
Electric vehicle and energy storage manufacturer Tesla has unveiled a new medium-voltage platform, with data centers among its target markets.

The Powercore system is a medium-voltage system that combines a solid-state transformer (SST), switchgear, and inverter in a single enclosure. According to the company, it is rated for 800VDC to 2,000VDC inputs and 10kV to 34.5kV AC, and can deliver up to 7.4MW of power at 34.5kV AC.

Tesla said that the product will be manufactured at its US facilities, with units expected to begin operating sometime next year. The company claimed that the units are designed for use in temperatures ranging from -40°C to 55°C (-40°F to 131°F) and carry a warranty of up to 25 years.

For the data center market, Tesla claimed that the Powercore system cuts out the multi-stage voltage step-down normally used to supply racks. Instead, the system takes power directly from the feeder, outputting power at 800VDC to the servers via a single conversion.

The company said it is already working with Nvidia to certify the system under the company’s DSX Ready program, which validates equipment for next-generation data centers. As of September, Tesla’s Megapack 2XL was one of three battery energy storage systems qualified under the program.

Tesla also said that Powercore can be paired with its Megapack batteries, using grid-forming controls to provide synthetic inertia and reactive power support.

AJ Booth, Tesla’s head of energy and charging, said this can smooth local voltage oscillations from dynamic data center loads.

“By adding a data center with Powercore and Megapack, we can provide a stiffer local grid and provide a more stable grid,” Booth told pv magazine USA. “It’s actually better than if you didn’t put a data center there at all, which is the amazing thing that batteries can do for the grid.”

Tesla claims Powercore includes what it calls the industry’s first built-in solid-state circuit breaker, which clears faults in 100 microseconds. Booth said this lets Tesla interrupt faults “a thousand times faster than traditional equipment.”

Elon Musk's company has pitched the platform as a way around conventional transformer supply chains, which have stretched up to four years due to massive demand from the data center market. In addition to the data center market, the product is being proposed as a solution for utility-scale solar, storage, and EV charging.

Tesla is the latest vendor to unveil a medium-voltage SST system for the data center market. Competitors include new players such as DG Matrix and Heron Power, alongside legacy power equipment manufacturers Eaton and Siemens.

stories.title: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and Sakura Internet sign MoU to establish sovereign AI infrastructure in Japan
stories.summary: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and internet service provider Sakura Internet have formalized plans to build sovereign AI infrastructure in Japan through a memorandum of understanding. The partnership aims to develop domestically controlled computing resources for AI workloads, reducing reliance on foreign cloud platforms.
stories.why_it_matters: Japan's pursuit of sovereign AI capabilities reflects a broader G7 trend toward data localization and technological autonomy, creating new opportunities for domestic industrial conglomerates while potentially fragmenting cloud market share currently held by US hyperscalers in a key Asia-Pacific market.
stories.title_zh: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries与Sakura Internet签署MoU，在日本建立sovereign AI基础设施
stories.summary_zh: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries与互联网服务提供商Sakura Internet已签署MoU，正式确定在日本建设sovereign AI基础设施的计划。该合作旨在开发用于AI工作负载的国内可控计算资源，减少对外国云平台的依赖。
stories.why_zh: 日本对sovereign AI能力的追求反映了G7国家中数据本地化和技术自主的广泛趋势，这为国内工业集团创造了新机遇，同时可能分散目前由美国hyperscale企业在这一关键亚太市场占据的云市场份额。
stories.content:
Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) and cloud provider and data center operator Sakura Internet have signed a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to establish sovereign AI and cloud infrastructure in Japan.

Under the MoU, the two will develop modular AI data centers that can be built efficiently and quickly, and look for opportunities to strengthen digital infrastructure in the country for sovereign AI workloads.

"As AI becomes national infrastructure, that infrastructure has to be resilient in both how it is built and how it is operated. With Sakura Internet, we want to give Japan a sovereign AI foundation that is secure, available when it matters, and fast enough to keep pace with demand. This is part of the MHI ITO(Note2) initiative: combining our strengths with the right partner to deliver value to far more customers," said Masayuki Suematsu, executive vice president and chief strategy officer, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries.

Kunihiro Tanaka, founder, CEO, and president, Sakura Internet, added: "With the rapid spread of AI, digital infrastructure such as cloud and data centers has become essential to society and industry. In this collaboration, we will combine MHI's technology and expertise in social infrastructure with our own experience building and operating cloud and data centers. Together, we aim to create new options for the domestic digital infrastructure that the sovereign AI and sovereign cloud era requires."

Earlier this year, MHI said that it was planning to revamp its gas turbine production process to drive output and cut manufacturing time to meet demand from the AI data center sector. The company launched an on-prem containerized data center offering in February.

Sakura Internet was selected by Japan's Digital Agency as a Government Cloud service provider for fiscal year 2026. It operates data centers in Tokyo, Osaka, and Hokkaido. Earlier this year, the company formed a consortium with NTT and Tokyu Land with plans to establish a data center cluster in Ishikari City in Hokkaido. Sakura Internet has operated its data center in Ishikari since 2011, and has recently been expanding and deploying GPUs at the site.

stories.title: Singapore's Racks Central to be acquired in reverse merger
stories.summary: Singaporean data center firm Racks Central is being acquired in a reverse merger.
stories.title_zh: 新加坡Racks Central将通过reverse merger被收购
stories.content:
Singaporean data center firm Racks Central is being acquired in a reverse merger.

Singapore Exchange (SGX)-listed Heptamax International Limited this week announced that it has entered into a sale and purchase agreement (SPA) with Racks Central Holdings Pte. Ltd. for the proposed acquisition of the entire issued and paid-up share capital of the Singaporean colocation firm.

The initial consideration for the sale shares is S$500 million (US$387.6 million). The deal is being structured as a reverse takeover of Heptamax, with the company issuing more than 800 million shares.

Founded in 2012, Racks Central operates a Tier III-quality carrier-neutral data center, located at 23 Tai Seng Drive. The facility has an IT capacity of approximately 8MW and has been in operation since 2014.

Racks Central’s revenue in 2025 was S$36.8 million (US$28.5m), with S$1.5 million in profit before tax.

The building the company operates out of is leased from AIMS APAC REIT. According to an AIMS annual report, Racks Central has around four years remaining on its lease for the six-story building.

Industrial solutions company Heptamax currently designs and builds customized automation systems and robotics solutions. Founded in 2008 as Great Group Holdings Limited, the company has operations in Singapore, Malaysia, Hong Kong, and China.

Heptamax said it believed that the proposed acquisition is of “commercial benefit” to the group and “represents an attractive investment opportunity to acquire an established data center developer and operator in Singapore, with a pathway to the Vendor’s data center projects in Malaysia… and to diversify and transform the group’s business.”

Upon the allotment and issuance of the maximum number of consideration shares, Racks Central Holdings Pte. Ltd. will hold more than 30 percent of the enlarged issued and paid-up share capital of Heptamax International Limited. As a result, Racks Central Holdings Pte. Ltd. will be obligated to make a mandatory general offer for all the Heptamax shares it does not own or control.

Earlier this year, APAC real estate firm ESR and the US$1 billion China‑ASEAN Investment Cooperation Fund II (CAF II) announced a strategic investment into Racks Central. The investment was set to support Racks Central’s overseas expansion, starting with Johor, Malaysia.

The company’s four-building campus in the Pasir Gudang area of Johor could total 510MW at full build-out. After breaking ground last year, the first 70MW RCJM1 facility is fully committed ahead of its targeted ready-for-service date in Q1 2027.

Racks Central has previously said it intends to build a 95MW campus on the Indonesian island of Batam, which is located south of Singapore across the Singapore Strait.

stories.title: Australian-run Nscale probes tech ties to blacklisted Chinese firm
stories.summary: Nscale, an Australian GPU cloud provider backed by investment firm Lakestar, is investigating its technology supply chain after revelations that at least one of its hardware vendors has ties to Sugon, a Chinese supercomputing firm on U.S. export control lists. The company, which recently rebranded from its previous identity, is racing to clarify whether its AI server procurement channels inadvertently violate American semiconductor restrictions.
stories.why_it_matters: For mid-sized GPU cloud operators outside the U.S. and China, the episode exposes how secondary and tertiary vendor relationships can trigger compliance landmines, jeopardizing access to Nvidia chips and American capital markets. It also signals that due diligence on supply chain provenance is becoming as critical as power and cooling in data center operations, with regulators and investors now scrutinizing hardware genealogy back to foundry level.
stories.title_zh: 澳大利亚运营的Nscale调查与被列入黑名单的中国公司的技术联系
stories.summary_zh: 由投资公司Lakestar支持的澳大利亚GPU云提供商Nscale正在调查其技术供应链，此前有披露显示其至少一家硬件供应商与中国超级计算公司Sugon有关联，而Sugon已被列入美国出口管制名单。这家最近重新品牌化的公司正在加紧澄清其AI服务器采购渠道是否无意中违反了美国半导体限制。
stories.why_zh: 对于美国和中国以外的中型GPU云运营商而言，这一事件暴露了二级和三级供应商关系如何触发合规地雷，危及获取Nvidia芯片和美国资本市场的机会。这也表明，对供应链来源的尽职调查正在变得与数据中心的电力和冷却同等关键，监管机构和投资者现在正将硬件谱系审查追溯到晶圆厂层面。
stories.content:
*London* | Upstart neocloud Nscale is examining the use of equipment in its data centres with links to a Chinese firm the US government has blacklisted.

The UK-based company, founded by Australian businessman Josh Payne, disclosed the potential supply chain issue in its updated prospectus filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, acknowledging it could cause project delays.

stories.summary: Engineering and building support company KJTS Group Bhd (KL:KJTS) said on Thursday it has secured a subcontract worth RM48 million involving mechanical works on a data centre in Port Dickson from the engineering and construction arm of Gamuda Bhd (KL:GAMUDA).

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.title_zh: KJTS获得Gamuda子公司4800万令吉数据中心相关工程分包合同
stories.content:
KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 19): Engineering and building support company KJTS Group Bhd (KL:KJTS) said on Thursday it has secured a subcontract worth RM48 million involving mechanical works on a data centre in Port Dickson from the engineering and construction arm of Gamuda Bhd (KL:GAMUDA).

In a bourse filing, the group said its wholly-owned unit KJ Technical Service Sdn Bhd entered into a subcontract agreement with Gamuda Engineering Sdn Bhd for the hyperscale data centre, which is being developed for a multinational technology company headquartered in the United States.

Under the contract, the group will undertake the mechanical package, covering the provision of materials, plant and labour necessary for the engineering, procurement, manufacture, delivery, installation, supervision, testing and commissioning, as well as maintenance and servicing of the mechanical systems.

The project is scheduled for completion in two phases, with Phase 1 slated to complete by Oct 22, 2027, and Phase 2 by Jan 21, 2028.

KJTS shares closed half a sen or 0.51% lower at 98 sen on Thursday, valuing the group at RM676.9 million.

stories.title: YTL Corp starts FY2027 with boost from construction, data centres
stories.summary: YTL Corp Bhd (KL:YTL) reported on Thursday a 6.4% increase in its first-quarter earnings thanks to higher construction activities, cement sales and cloud services.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.title_zh: YTL Corp凭借建筑和数据中心业务增长开启2027财年
stories.content:
KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 19): YTL Corp Bhd (KL:YTL) reported on Thursday a 6.4% increase in its first-quarter earnings thanks to higher construction activities, cement sales and cloud services.

Net profit was RM368.58 million for the three months ended Sept 30, 2026 (1QFY2027) compared with RM346.48 million in the same quarter a year earlier, according to an exchange filing. Revenue for the quarter increased 34% year-on-year to above RM10 billion for the first time.

The newly-started artificial intelligence cloud services provided YTL Corp with a shot in the arm for the quarter. Construction earnings, meanwhile, nearly quadrupled year-on-year from higher progress billings and better margins.

YTL Corp, which controls Malayan Cement Bhd (KL:MCEMENT), said the outlook for the construction and infrastructure sectors in Malaysia remains encouraging, supporting demand for its building materials.

However, the company flagged external risks from swings in energy prices, transportation costs, and other production related expenses.

YTL Power International Bhd (KL:YTLPOWR), its listed multi-utilities arm, reported an 8% decline in earnings as lower power generation margins overshadowed growth in its data-centre business.

Net profit for 1QFY2027 was RM460.62 million, down from RM500.57 million, due to lower retail margin at its power business while its water division suffered from higher maintenance costs and weaker earnings from the UK.

Data centres at YTL Power saw a jump in pre-tax profit as data halls operations ramped up and boosted the segment’s revenue by nearly six times.

Looking ahead, YTL Power said it is looking to expand beyond Kulai Data Centre Park after investing RM13.5 billion in the business. The plan for now, is to increase the park’s capacity to 1,200 megawatts, of which 298MW is already contracted.

None of the listed YTL companies declared a dividend for the quarter.

Shares of YTL Corp declined two sen or 1% to RM1.71 on Thursday, valuing the group at over RM20 billion. YTL Power, meanwhile, was unchanged at RM4, giving it a market capitalisation of RM35 billion.

stories.title: Arm CEO Haas approached by Nvidia board's recruitment firm to replace Jensen Huang
stories.summary: The process of reaching out to executives amid a search for Jensen Huang’s replacement has begun
stories.title_zh: Nvidia董事会招聘公司接触Arm CEO Haas以接替Jensen Huang
stories.content:
The process of reaching out to executives amid a search for Jensen Huang’s replacement has begun

ARM CHIEF executive officer Rene Haas has been approached regarding the CEO role at Nvidia by recruiting firm Heidrick & Struggles, which was hired by the board to recommend a replacement for Jensen Huang, according to a person familiar with the process.

Heidrick & Struggles has begun the process of reaching out to executives who might be able to take on the job after Huang left the company last week, according to the person, who asked not to be identified because the process is not public.

Nvidia and Arm representatives did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Nvidia, the world’s largest chipmaker, cut ties with Huang on Nov 12, after revelations about his extramarital affairs spurred a widening scandal.

Huang has admitted to a relationship with a woman that the US government has investigated for spying on behalf of China. Beijing has denied the espionage plot.

Hiring Haas would bring in someone with a history at Nvidia. He served for seven years at the company as general manager of computing products.

Nvidia also attempted to acquire Arm in 2020, though the merger eventually broke down in the face of regulatory opposition.

But the 64-year-old Haas – or anyone else stepping into the Nvidia CEO role – would come under intense pressure. It is arguably the highest-profile job in the tech industry, and the new leader will need to confront a corporate culture shaped around the personality of one man: Huang.

Haas spoke about Huang’s departure during a tech conference in Austin on Wednesday (Nov 18), describing his old boss as “a legend”.

“What he built at Nvidia is historic,” Haas said. “You don’t have many champions like that.” BLOOMBERG

stories.title: Lenovo posts 48% revenue jump on AI-related sales, beating estimates
stories.summary: Its revenue rises to US$30.2 billion, above an LSEG consenus estimate of US$27.6 billion
stories.title_zh: Lenovo AI相关销售推动收入增长48%，超出预期
stories.content:
Its revenue rises to US$30.2 billion, above an LSEG consenus estimate of US$27.6 billion

\[BEIJING\] China’s Lenovo reported a 48 per cent jump in second-quarter revenue, beating analyst estimates, on strong growth in artificial intelligence-related sales such as servers and other hardware.

Revenue rose to US$30.2 billion, above an LSEG consenus estimate of US$27.6 billion drawn from six analysts.

Under Hong Kong accounting standards, the company posted a net loss of US$640 million, compared with a net profit of US$340 million a year earlier.

But Lenovo also said that it booked, under different accounting standards, adjusted net profit of US$1.4 billion, up 166 per cent.

The adjusted figure strips out non-cash accounting items linked to warrants and convertible bonds that Lenovo issued as part of its strategic partnership with Alat, a manufacturing and technology company in Saudi Arabia.

The Infrastructure Solutions Group, which makes servers and data centre equipment, had its strongest quarter ever, with revenue climbing 178 per cent year on year to US$11.3 billion.

AI-related revenue rose 79 per cent to US$10.8 billion, comprising 36 per cent of the group’s total revenue.

Lenovo’s personal computer, tablet and smartphone division, which accounted for about 60 per cent of total revenue during the quarter, grew 15 per cent. REUTERS

stories.title: Trump hails 'great' ties with Xi, downplays Nvidia scandal
stories.summary: Expectations are low for major breakthroughs, as they are meeting again in December
stories.title_zh: 特朗普称赞与习近平"良好"关系，淡化NVIDIA丑闻
stories.content:
Expectations are low for major breakthroughs, as they are meeting again in December

\[SHENZHEN\] US President Donald Trump hailed his great “friendship” with Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping and downplayed a spying scandal involving Nvidia, just hours before leaders of the world’s top two economies meet for talks in China.

“I was with President Xi all night last night, sitting next to him at the dinner, right on his right hand side, and we spoke the whole evening,” he told Fox News on Thursday on the sidelines of this week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in the southern city of Shenzhen.

When asked if the downfall of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, a prominent opponent of restrictions on chip sales to China, came up in conversation with Xi at a banquet on Wednesday evening, Trump said: “I might have referred to it just briefly because it’s such a tragedy.”

Trump is slated to hold his third summit of the year with Xi later on Thursday, with the fallout from the Nvidia scandal threatening to upend a fragile trade truce set to expire on Jan 10.

Washington unleashed new chip curbs earlier this week designed to thwart Beijing’s ability to train frontier artificial intelligence models, prompting Beijing to warn of countermeasures if the two sides cannot reach a resolution.

Despite the underlying tensions, Xi personally greeted Trump upon the US president’s arrival at the airport on Wednesday, returning a favour for Trump’s in-person welcome when the Chinese leader visited Washington in September.

The unusual gesture marked the first time in roughly 50 years that a Chinese leader met a visiting dignitary on the tarmac.

Trump lauded that welcome and sought to downplay reports that Huang had conducted an affair with a Chinese executive that US intelligence believes was spying for China.

“Any pretty woman that comes from China, they considered her to be a spy,” he told Fox. “She was a businesswoman who bought chips.”

Beyond the airport pageantry, expectations are low for major breakthroughs, given both leaders are meeting again at the Group of 20 leaders’ summit in Miami in December.

The two sides are looking to advance tariff reductions on US$30 billion worth of each other’s imports, negotiated under the newly established US-China Board of Trade. A similar framework has been floated for bilateral investment, though progress has been slow.

Xi urged Apec members to reduce barriers to trade and investment in his opening remarks at the leaders’ meeting on Thursday morning, calling for an “open, fair, just and non-discriminatory environment for cooperation”.

Trump and Xi are also expected to meet with Russian leader Vladimir Putin this afternoon in what would be an unprecedented summit between the three men, who together control at least 90 per cent of the world’s nuclear weapons.

In 2025, Trump and Xi reached a truce to end their trade war, and agreed to extend it to early next year during their September meeting in Washington.

Under that deal, in which both sides agreed to tariff reductions, an understanding was reached for the Trump administration to hold off imposing new tech curbs against Beijing in exchange for a steady flow of critical minerals from China.

That bargain has increasingly come under strain. US officials have repeatedly complained that America is not getting rare earths at the expected volume and pace – a grievance US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer raised with Chinese Vice-Premier He Lifeng in a video call earlier in November.

The US Commerce Department this week published interim rules that would restrict China’s remote access to high-end AI chips hosted in overseas data centers.

If thoroughly enforced, the regulation could deal a heavy blow to China’s AI ecosystem by shutting off a crucial source of computing power for Chinese developers racing to build cutting-edge models. The move drew a sharp rebuke from China’s commerce ministry.

The Xi-Trump meetings this year have been more about atmospherics and keeping the broad relationship stable than substantive negotiations on trade, investment and security matters.

Asked how the American people can tell if Thursday’s meeting is a success, Trump told Fox News: “I think I’ve already gotten that headline, because the relationship that I have with China is a great one.”

“The fanfare, the beauty, the pageantry, the thousands of people, the young children, the soldiers, the whole thing – it was a great respect, and I appreciate that,” Trump said. “That’s a big win for us. It’s a big win for China, too.” BLOOMBERG

stories.title: CoolIT & Ecolab launch 3MW CDU
stories.summary: CoolIT and Ecolab have launched a new high-capacity cooling distribution unit (CDU) for liquid-cooled data centers.
stories.title_zh: CoolIT 和 Ecolab 推出 3MW CDU
stories.content:
CoolIT and Ecolab have launched a new high-capacity cooling distribution unit (CDU) for liquid-cooled data centers.

Ecolab this week announced CoolIT’s new CHx 3000 CDU. The liquid-to-liquid, row- and facility-based CDU delivers 3MW of cooling at a 3°C (37.4**°**F) approach temperature difference. Its dual heat exchangers support 45°C (113**°**F) warm-water operations.

CoolT’s highest-capacity CDU to date, the company said it was able to provide direct-to-chip cooling to support high-density hardware such as Vera Rubin GPUs: the CHx3000 could cool up to 18 racks per CDU at 190kW per rack.

Consuming 75kW of power, the new CDU includes Ecolab’s 3D TRASAR technology, providing built-in continuous coolant health monitoring.

Units will be available to ship beginning Q1 2027.

"AI is advancing at an extraordinary pace, and the infrastructure behind it needs to advance just as fast," said Christophe Beck, chairman, president and CEO of Ecolab. "That's exactly what we're enabling today. For too long, cooling hardware, fluid management and digital technology have operated separately. We're bringing them together to help our customers get more computing power, faster, while using less water and energy. And we're just getting started."

Ecolab’s 3D TRASAR Technology continuously monitors coolant quality in the cooling loop that serves the IT equipment, including temperature, differential pressure, pH, conductivity, turbidity, flow rate, and glycol concentration.

This week also saw Ecolab announce a partnership with Siemens to combine the former’s liquid-cooling and CDU technology with Siemens’ power distribution, automation, software, and digital twin capabilities.

Ecolab also said it was working with Alfa Laval for its heat exchanger and flow components expertise for the new CoolIT CHx 3000 CDU.

Ecolab’s virtual twin technology has been developed in collaboration with Dassault Systèmes, and aims to link Technology Cooling System (TCS) and facility water system (FWS) models to simulate AI data center performance.

Founded in 1923 to sell carpet cleaning products, NYSE-listed Ecolab provides water treatment and monitoring products and services across industries, including food, healthcare, hospitality, and manufacturing.

It launched a data center-centric version of its 3D TRASAR water monitoring product for liquid cooling in 2025 and launched its own liquid cooling portfolio later that year. The company acquired CoolIT from KKR earlier this year.
